title: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
why: A-type robot-agent harness that keeps robot skills frozen and learns local placement/requirement scope from human feedback. Physical success is recorded separately from requirement satisfaction; a scope ladder mixes memory, explicit rules, and a learner, and is compared with language-model agents that have persistent memory in camera-grounded robot simulations.
mechanism: CRAFT (Contextual Requirement Adaptation with Frozen Tools) does not retrain skills. When a person rejects a placement, a scope ladder first reuses memory if the same action was already judged in a nearly identical situation; otherwise it combines memory, explicit rules, and a learner for requirements beyond those rules, weighting each by how well it predicted earlier feedback. Evaluation keeps execution failures and timeouts in the score and uses generated requirements with simulated feedback.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): controlled studies show gains over correction memory alone on a utility that rewards acceptable actions and charges mistakes and questions. In camera-grounded robot simulations, the ladder asks fewer questions than language-model agents with persistent memory, but some of those agents take fewer wrong actions and succeed more often after requirements change. All evidence is from simulation. Numeric tables unread.

title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
why: A-type agentic navigation harness that keeps goal ownership in an Agent, authorizes only a bounded action set, stores evidence memory, and triggers an event-driven verifier (Jev) after blocked or failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments, with freshness/once-only checks and a real quadruped deployment.
mechanism: The Agent plans from RGB, odometry, memory, and feedback and authorizes a bounded action set. Jev reviews structured evidence after blocked/failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments; version, freshness, and once-only checks govern whether a decision is applied. A single executor and an independent RGB reflex constrain motion, and goal revisions revoke obsolete requests before replanning.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across six simulated task families, AgenticJevNav achieves 73.33% success over 60 trials, 21.67 percentage points above the next-best Agent-only aggregate control (the authors note differing historical protocols). A real-world GENISOM L1 quadruped deployment achieves 70.0% success over 30 trials, including bounded search reporting. Numeric tables beyond the abstract unread.

title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
why: A-type agentic VLN system (LeaP-VLN) with explicit plan-execute-verify-recover cycles: an independent progress verifier gates subtask completion and triggers dual-phase recovery, and the executor is co-trained on progress reasoning plus expert action corrections so it can run in that closed-loop interface.
mechanism: LeaP-VLN couples a progress-aware executor with an independent progress verifier. The verifier checks subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery on route deviation. The executor is trained in two stages: behavior cloning on expert demonstrations, then joint training on demonstrations, expert action corrections, and progress-reasoning supervision, including policy-generated trajectories that expose intra-subtask drift and inter-subtask state shifts.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE are claimed to reach state-of-the-art success rates among monocular methods trained without additional navigation datasets, and the authors say real-world experiments further validate LeaP-VLN on long-horizon navigation. Numeric tables, baselines, and trial counts unread.

title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
why: B-type diagnostic benchmark for vision-language embodied agents that act through skill-level tools on causal hospital task chains in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, reporting where a chain breaks, what the agent does after a failed call, and how far its position estimate drifts; the authors also plan to release the evaluation harness and a scripted solvability robot.
mechanism: Ten hospital chores in Isaac Sim each have two unscored warm-up steps followed by a causal chain of five scored sub-tasks in one continuous simulation, so the state left by one step (object pose, a choice, or a fact seen once) determines the next. Vision-language agents act through skill-level tools from camera images. A scripted robot that makes only the calls a model gets is the solvability check. The benchmark reads from each trajectory where the chain breaks, the post-failure call, and position-estimate drift.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): this version reports first results only — 15 of 60 planned runs (three models at high effort, one run each on chores T1 and T10 from both start states and T3 from one), with scripted-robot proofs on three of the ten chores. Of the 15 runs, 2 passed all five sub-tasks. Runs still going after sub-tasks 1 to 5 were 15, 8, 4, 2, 2. Of 189 failed calls, 168 were followed by a different call and 111 by a call that did not fail. The authors state these are first results and not a full benchmark.

title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
why: A-type harness that lets API-only frozen frontier multimodal models use contact force without demonstrations or finetuning: self-terminating force primitives close the force loop beneath the model, and a physics translation layer returns quantities with uncertainty as the tool result, evaluated on a real arm and on ForceBench / HiddenPhys.
mechanism: After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or from joint torques alone, ForceHarness runs self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event, so the slow API model is not in the inner force loop. A physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. The authors also introduce HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables, to compare the harness with expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations are said to show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values. Numeric tables unread.

title: Self-Calibrating Vision-Agent-Action: Deploying Pick-and-Place to New Robot Cells without Demonstrations or Fine-Tuning
why: A-type vision-language / language-model agent (VAA) for pick-and-place that self-calibrates command maps, camera geometry and lens distortion from its own motion and fingertips, then plans grasps from measured object depth, without robot demonstrations or fine-tuning, and is compared with frozen VLAs on changed LIBERO cells.
mechanism: Vision-Agent-Action uses pre-trained vision-language and language models for interpretation, measures the command map and camera geometry from its own motion and fingertips, estimates lens distortion, and plans grasps from measured object depth. A controlled study of eight public LIBERO-fine-tuned VLAs varies robot hardware, camera geometry, appearance, and base frame; gripper and frame changes dominate their losses in the tested fractional design.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across 18 cells with gripper or base-frame changes, frozen VAA achieves 230/360 successes (64%), the refined VAA 268/360 (74%), and the strongest released VLA on this subset 76/360 (21%). Paired ablations are said to support the self-calibration bundle, lens estimation under compounded changes, and the measured-depth pipeline. On a two-step LIBERO-Goal chain with object state carried between instructions, VAA completes 54/60 chains in changed cells, while four evaluated VLAs complete none. Numeric tables unread.

title: RoboCoEvo: Expanding Robot Capabilities through Agent-Policy Co-Evolution
why: A-type failure-guided co-evolution between an MLLM agent and a robotic foundation model (VLA): the agent writes and revises code-as-policy failure-detection and recovery programs that generate corrective experience, the VLA is post-trained on that experience, and the updated failure distribution then guides the next program revision, evaluated on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin.
mechanism: RoboCoEvo couples refinement of the agent's explicit, reusable executable knowledge with parameter learning in a robotic foundation model. Through a code-as-policy formulation, the agent develops and refines executable failure-detection and recovery programs that generate targeted corrective experience. Post-training consolidates those corrective behaviors into the end-to-end VLA policy. Changes in the updated policy's failure distribution then guide subsequent revisions of the agent's programs.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): experiments on BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, and RoboTwin demonstrate sustained improvements in autonomous VLA task performance across successive co-evolution rounds. Numeric tables, baselines, and round-wise scores unread.

why: Update of the known H2E (Harness-to-Executor) paper already in the corpus: v2 expands the abstract from a REVERIE-CE-only report to also name NavRAG-CE, second-round recovery sessions, and a claim that the distilled VLA exceeds its training agent on unseen episodes with zero LLM tokens.

The method remains session-level distillation of an LLM planner plus frozen VLA into a VLA that runs alone at test time, with loss masking on steps that move away from the goal and end labels near the goal. v2 comments explicitly add NavRAG-CE results, second-round recovery sessions, and an extended appendix; the v2 abstract also states that the distilled VLA exceeds its agent on unseen episodes.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abstract): H2E sets a new state of the art on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE. It raises an 8B VLA's success rate by 15.6% and 11.1% respectively, surpassing methods trained on 10M samples. The distilled VLA exceeds its agent on unseen episodes with zero LLM tokens and runs 3.7 times faster. The v1 abstract reported only REVERIE-CE val-unseen (3,189 episodes), raising an 8B VLA from 35.0% to 44.9% success, and did not name NavRAG-CE or the exceed-the-agent claim. title: Consensus Within, Competition Between: Decentralized LLM Teams for Perimeter Defense
why: Update of the known decentralized LLM perimeter-defense paper already in the corpus: the v2 abstract expands the network-condition results from 'only limited radio range changed a team's breach rate' to quantified effects of burst message loss, falsified reports, and limited radio range on commander vs consensus-team breach rates, and the comments add a data URL and more supplementary pages.
mechanism: Corpus/latest known version is 2610.41044v1 (submitted Thu, 29 Oct 2026). The Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 replacement listing announced v2 (submitted Sat, 14 Nov 2026 20:07:35 UTC). The study still compares a central commander, an auction-based consensus team, and independent LLM agents in a simplified perimeter-defense simulation, including unreliable communication and visual disguise probes. v2's abstract restates the same headline breach rates but adds a finer breakdown of how burst message loss, falsified reports, and limited radio range affect the commander versus the consensus team.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abstract): breach rates remain 15% for the consensus team, 32% for the commander and 29% for independent agents. Burst message loss, falsified reports and limited radio range raised the commander's breach rate by 10 to 18 percentage points, whereas the consensus team's changed by at most 5. The v1 abstract instead said that of the different network conditions, only limited radio range changed a team's breach rate, raising the commander's. Other reported figures (the 38-point bid-authority effect; disguise/forewarning rates) appear in both abstracts. Comments grow from 88 pages (33 main + 55 supplementary) to 97 pages (37 main + 60 supplementary) and add a data URL.
